definitions.short: the eagle (or other large bird of prey)
definitions.full: H5404. nesher נֶשֶׁר noun masculine Deut 32:11 griffon-vulture, eagle (Late Hebrew id. ; Assyrian našru ; נַשְׁרָא ᵑ7 ; Syriac Arabic vulture (Lane 2780 ), vulgar Ethiopic Di 641 ; Sabean נסר proper name, of deity, and נסר ביתן DHM ZMG. xxix (1875), 600 ; xxxvii (1883), 356); — absolute ׳נ Hosea 8:1 +; נָָֽשֶׁד Deut 28:49 +; plural נְשָׁרִים 2Sam 1:23 +, construct נִשְׁרֵי Lam 4:19 ; — sometimes (perhaps not always) the griffon-vulture (Tristr NHB 172 ff. Dr Deut 14:12 Now Archi i. 84 Lane 2780 ), Micah 1:16 (bald, in simile) flying swiftly to pery Hab 1:8 ; Job 9:26 , compare Prov 30:17 ( ׳בְּנֵינֿ , unclean Lev 11:13 ; Deut 14:12 ; soaring Job 30:27 , also in simile Prov 23:5 ; Isa 40:31 ; Obadiah 4, building nest high Jer 49:16 (compare also Job 39:27 ); as swift also 2Sam 1:23 , especially of Babylonian and Assyr. invader Jer 4:13 ; Lam 4:19 , compare Hosea 8:1 ; Deut 28:49 ; Jer 48:40 ; 49:22 (all in comparisons), הַגָּדוֺל הַנֶּשֶׁר Ezek 17:3 (figurativeof Nebuch.), 17:7 (figurative of king of Egypt); leaving no trace of light Prov 30:19 ; as renewing youth (by moulting) Psa 103:5 ; as training and supporting its young Exod 19:4 (E), Deut 32:11 (song); נ ׳מְּני of cherubim in vision Ezek 1:10 ; 10:4 . — Only Micah 1:16 seems to compel reference to vulture (on eating fresh carrion by eagles see references in Di Lev 11:13 ), and ׳נ may be a more comprehensive word, including both vulture and eagle.
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to lacerate;
